requirements.requirement: A persistent host firewall is enabled on node1 and recovers after restart.
requirements.summary: Firewalld was active and enabled before restart, with the intended runtime and permanent policy. The acknowledged reboot changed the boot ID, after which firewalld and sshd were active/enabled and the policy, nftables rules, and functional behavior had recovered.

requirements.requirement: Inbound SSH and TCP port 8080 are permitted.
requirements.summary: The active and permanent public zone permits SSH and 8080/tcp. Effective nftables rules accept TCP ports 22 and 8080; sshd is listening, and an isolated ingress test received HTTP 200 on port 8080 both before and after reboot.

The public zone has a REJECT target and effective nftables input policy rejects unmatched traffic. Isolated ingress tests to unrelated TCP port 9090 were rejected before and after reboot despite an existing listener on that port.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The system remained CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64. The implementation used the already-installed native firewalld/nftables packages, and package health remained intact.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The firewall persistently permits SSH and TCP 8080, rejects unrelated inbound traffic, survives a directly observed reboot, and leaves the OS release and kernel unchanged. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and corroborated by the fixed boot-identity observations. Only minor temporary test-file residue detracts from operational hygiene.
limitations: SSH permission was demonstrated through the active accept rule, listening sshd service, and post-reboot recovery, but no separate end-to-end SSH connection probe was captured.
The lifecycle collector inventories /tmp only in bounded form; it confirms the six named test artifacts but does not provide their sizes or contents.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had a clear role: the permanent firewalld changes established the requested policy, the bounded namespace/veth changes tested ingress and were covered by cleanup traps, and the reboot fulfilled the mandatory evidence protocol. No unrelated system mutation or failed service was observed. The sole hygiene defect was retained test residue: the two functional tests created six firewall test log/output files under /tmp and did not remove them. These unnecessary retained artifacts were caused by cmd-4c5765297c464a40 and cmd-1fd00035722e4545. Package health remained good and no failed services appeared.
